item.title: 16-year-old SATA II SSD survives 1 petabyte of writes, 25x the drive's rating
item.description:
📝 However, just as older cars may require more frequent maintenance and become less predictable over time, SSDs that surpass their TBW threshold may gradually become less reliable. It would seem that the user created a workload that kept making cached writes to the SSD. However, this particular case was pretty interesting, given that it was on an older drive with MLC NAND that has since disappeared from the market.
🔗 Read more: https://www.tomshardware.com/pc-components/ssds/16-year-old-sata-ii-ssd-survives-1-petabyte-of-writes-25x-over-the-drives-tbw-rating

item.title: Lithuanian startup launches open-source network to detect Shahed-type drones
item.description:
📝 19 13:25 Shahed drone | AP,AP A startup, together with activists, has launched an open-source drone detection system that links data from participating volunteers’ phones, according to a press release from the Drone Rada (Dronuradaras. The goal is to build the largest civic acoustic drone detection network in the Baltic region, with 10,000 active participants. The Drone Radar team is also discussing potential cooperation with Lithuania's major mobile network operators, with a view to installing sensors on their telecommunications towers.
🔗 Read more: https://www.lrt.lt/en/news-in-english/19/2965205/lithuanian-startup-launches-open-source-network-to-detect-shahed-type-drones

item.title: From PGP to Mythos: a brief history of export controls that didn't stop anyone
item.description:
📝 The idea was to classify surveillance and hacking software as dual-use, thus forcing spyware makers to get export licenses to sell their products abroad. Since then, other countries in Europe have been lax with spyware makers like Italy. Despite numerous scandals, Europe, home to many spyware and hacking tools makers, has continually failed to curb the export of spyware to authoritarian regimes.
🔗 Read more: https://techcrunch.com/2026/06/19/encryption-spyware-and-now-mythos-history-shows-why-cyber-export-control-doesnt-work/
